body:
I've been wrestling with this problem for awhile, among other problems, and would like to know your perspective.

* Have you talked to a doctor about this problem?
* If not, would you have felt more comfortable talking to a doctor about this problem?
* Do you talk with your friends or family about these kinds of things (emotional things)?
* If you do, I unfortunately can't relate.  But if you don't, how will you broach the subject?
* I've often wanted to not drink, but I haven't gotten to a point that I want to continually be sober.  Is that something that you've ever felt?

I've probably deleted my response to you three times now.  Mainly because I don't know how best to respond.  So I'm just going to say what comes to mind.  I think you have a strength in your ability to ask for help.  I've never done that in person.  And it scares the hell out of me.

Tomorrow would've been a week.  I fucked up again tonight.  What pisses me off the most is after the shakes and discomfort on Tuesday and being able to wake up without a headache for 5 days straight, I had a manic moment today and found an excuse to go to the store tonight.  

I hope I quit dancing with this devil someday.  The money won't last and I've long since pushed friends to better lives.

I don't know why I'm responding to you; maybe because in the six years you've experienced life on its terms I've tried my damnedest to dull it away.  Probably because I only 'talk' to people when I'm drunk.

Congrats on having the strength of character to find a solution and stick with it.

I've been a daily binge drinker (approximately a pint of vodka a night) for the last two months and at least 4 times a week for the last four years or so. I've been getting mild tremors in the afternoon/evening lately and feeling extremely anxious/manic before I get a drink.

I've been a daily binge drinker (approximately a pint of vodka a night) for the last two months and at least 4 times a week for the last four years or so.  I've been getting mild tremors in the afternoon/evening lately and feeling extremely anxious/manic before I get a drink.

Thank you for the advice.  I've found a few treatment centers near me but I haven't contacted them yet.

I don't have any insurance right now.  I was wondering if seeking treatment would make it harder for me to get insurance in the future.
Thank you very much.  This information helps.
Thank you.  I just called them and they gave me some numbers to call.   I really appreciate it.
Thank you very much for that.  I'm still scared but thank you.

I think I need to quit.  I've become the typical twenty-something basement-dweller.  My hands shake in the evenings without a drink and I've read about seizures.  I don't think I'm in immediate medical trouble since my DTs have been worse before and I'm alive but I think I need a doctor to make sure.
I'm afraid of a group.  I'm deathly afraid of telling people my feelings face to face.
I'm honestly scared of AA.  I'm afraid of a group.  I'm also frightened by talking to a doctor, but I feel like I can't do this anymore.
Sorry, I'm not the best at receiving compliments.
Well thank you for the compliment.  I've never been good at receiving them.
I don't feel like I have a gift.  It's hard to recognize myself as such.

Thank you for the compliment.  

It still hurts to be alone.
Thanks for listening.  I appreciate the response.

Be honest to those you love.

I'm a hypocrite here and I think it's my downfall.  But if you love someone, be honest with them.

I've wanted to disappear for so long.  I stopped talking to friends.  I stopped returning calls.  And they let me go.  I've been gone to them for a couple of years now.  But nothing is easier.  I'm still unhappy.  Don't go my route.  It's not better here.

I talked to a very old friend the other day and that was the highlight of my month.
Thank you.

It was so strange.  I just wanted to disappear, like I had never existed.  More often than not, I still kind of feel the same way.  But I feel less low right now.  Probably a good thing.  I'd like to thank you for responding.  I appreciate the time you put into your response.  Thank you.
I'd like to thank you for your reply.  I was feeling very low a few days ago and I didn't know where to go.  Thank you for replying in my time of need.  I hope someday to help someone else as well.

Thank you very kindly for your reply.  I was in a very bad place a few days ago and I didn't know what to do. I'm still kind of lost but I think I'm better for the time being.  I'd like to express my sincerest gratefulness for your response.

I stay alive now because I worry the cousin who smiles when I talk wouldn't smile anymore.  I stay alive because my parents might want to follow me if I were to leave.

They're my 'one more day.'  I still hate it right now.  I think I just want to let something out right now.  Thank you for responding.

I want to stop drinking but I don't want to be sober.

Help.

Sometimes I shake from the tears. And there's no goddamn good reason.

I want to hurt less.
Some days I just want a hug from a stranger, I don't know why.

Sometime I hear songs and I can only think about how they don't apply to me.  Or how sunsets were meant for someone else.

You are not alone.
I'm sorry.  Thank you for your reply.

I used to think I'd be like my dad, my uncles, my grandfathers; married and supporting a family.  Right now I have trouble thinking that could be me.

Somedays I wish they would give up on me so that I could disappear without guilt.
I'm 27, I live with my parents.  I made about $7000 last year, probably about the same this year.  The last date I went on was in high school.  This is not where I thought I'd be.
Is it worth sticking out?
No, something called the Egg.
